column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the reply’s speaker unnamed and uses verbless comparisons; BSB names Jehoshaphat and adds we will join you.
The Hebrew says today; BSB uses first.
The Hebrew switches from shall we go to shall I refrain; BSB uses we for both.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the LORD can be sought through the man and includes all his days; BSB says the man can ask the LORD and uses only bad.
The Hebrew calls the summoned man a eunuch without an ownership expression; BSB says one of his officials.
The Hebrew repeats sitting and calls the clothing garments without royal; BSB omits the repetition and adds royal.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew links the promise with and; BSB uses for.
The Hebrew retains one mouth and singular your word; BSB uses one accord and plural words.
The Hebrew says whatever my God says without an explicit to me; BSB adds tells me.
The Hebrew leaves Micaiah unnamed as arriver and replier and switches from we go to I refrain; BSB names him and keeps both questions plural.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and uses plural masters; BSB names Micaiah and uses singular master.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB names Micaiah.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the final speaker unnamed; BSB identifies him as the LORD.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says cheek; BSB uses face.
The Hebrew says behold and a room within a room; BSB adds soon and condenses the rooms to an inner room.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats distress with bread and water and says in peace; BSB adds only and uses safely.
The Hebrew addresses all peoples; BSB uses all you people.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says garments without royal and has plural they entered battle; BSB adds royal and has the king enter alone.
Close to the Hebrew.
